channel.title: The Lowndes Signal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Lowndes Signal (lowndessignal.com)

item.title: Fort Deposit officials take oath of office
item.description: After a contentious election, Fort Deposit swears in Mayor Madelene Means and town council, pledging unity, new ideas and regular town halls to shape the town's future.

item.title: Lowndes Head Start attends national association
item.description: Lowndes County Head Start parents and staff join NHSA’s 2025 Parent and Family Engagement Conference in Orlando to explore new early childhood development resources.

item.title: What's Happening in Lowndes County
item.description: Lowndes County offers free weather prep session, parenting and mom classes, school jobs, pre-K and Head Start sign-ups, septic aid, veteran meetups and more local resources.

item.title: Central Elementary launches inaugural Beta Club chapter
item.description: Central Elementary inducts nine 4th- and 5th-graders into Lowndes County’s first National Beta Club chapter, promoting scholarship, leadership, character and service.

item.title: Sewell accepting summer internship applications
item.description: Rep. Terri Sewell seeks college students and recent grads for summer 2026 internships in her D.C. and district offices; applications due March 27 at 5 p.m. CST.

item.title: New council holds first meeting
item.description: Fort Deposit’s new town council holds first meeting, naming key officials, setting its meeting schedule, choosing banks and ratifying poll workers after the Jan. 13 election.

item.title: Of choir robes and swing sets
item.description: A pastor recalls turning down choir robes and a playground request, and how those choices reshaped his view of church priorities, compromise and keeping focus on ministry.

item.title: The holy season of Lent
item.description: As Ash Wednesday on Feb. 18 begins Lent’s 40 days of prayer and repentance, local Methodist churches invite all to reflect, fast and seek deeper faith.

item.title: Seawright represents Alabama FBLA at State Capitol
item.description: Central, Hayneville senior Jakayden Seawright, a 17-year-old FBLA district vice president and teen business owner, represented Alabama FBLA at a State Capitol proclamation signing.

item.title: Athlete contest opens round 21
item.description: Vote hourly for Lowndes County Athlete of the Week: Jerdarius Davis, Ellis Ann Evans and Makayla Saffold; winners get pizza, cupcakes and advance to April’s Athlete of the Year contest.
